draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kadamakkudy! It's a cluster of fourteen islands about 8 km north of Kochi city centre, and people call it the Kuttanad of Kochi.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat out on the islands, so save your appetite for Ernakulam or ask a local.

moodReplies.show-me-around: You're a few minutes from the heart of the islands. Veeranpuzha, the northern stretch of Vembanad Lake, is about a 16 min walk, and Chathanad is a short drive over the new bridge.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet spot by Veeranpuzha, where wide paddy fields stretch out with hardly any houses around.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Hardly anyone lives along Veeranpuzha's paddy fields, because there's no fresh water to be had there.

spots.name: Kadamakkudy Islands
spots.detail: 3 min walk · Fourteen islands, one village

spots.name: Veeranpuzha
spots.detail: 16 min walk · Lake and open paddy fields

spots.name: Chathanad
spots.detail: Short drive · Across the Kadamakkudy–Chathanad bridge

tips.title: Count the islands.
tips.body: Valiya Kadamakudy is the main island, and the others include Moolampilly, Pizhala and Kothad.

tips.title: Use the new bridge.
tips.body: The Kadamakkudy–Chathanad bridge is now the main road link to North Paravur.

story.title: A venerable priest
story.body: Mar Varghese Payyappilly Palakkappilly, now called Venerable, served as parish priest of Valiya Kadamakkudy Syrian Catholic Church.

story.title: Ferries on the lake
story.body: Regular ferries ran from Munambam to Ernakulam across Veeranpuzha, the old Kadakkarakkayal.

story.title: Island life
story.body: The census counted 15,823 people across the islands, with literacy well above the national average.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Nine Catholic churches, quiet paddy fields and a new bridge. Pick an island and wander.
